rows.A_note: Level 1 is met: EV-050 acknowledges environmental impact in policy and EV-051 shows no system assessed. EV-052 and EV-053 do not separate AI energy use, so there is nothing for level 3.
rows.B_note: Policy clause exists but no assessment for any system; evidence establishes absence

rows.A_note: The curriculum is role-based (EV-090), but incomplete coverage scores level 1 under the coverage definition. Level 3 tracking against targets is not evidenced: EV-091 gives completion counts with no stated targets.
rows.B_note: Completion and competency are tracked, but no report against targets; evidence supports level 2 but not level 3

rows.A_note: The meeting cadence part of level 2 is met: EV-101 shows all four quarterly meetings held, with attendance and quorum recorded. The decision-log gap alone drops the score to 1. EV-103 shows strategy oversight, but level 3 measures of items decided are not evidenced.
rows.B_note: Committee charter, minutes, and decision log exist, but no measure of AI items decided or cycle report; evidence supports level 2 but not level 3

rows.A_note: Level 1 is met by EV-130 (campaign). Level 3 would also fail: EV-131/EV-133 give survey values and two data points but no stated targets and no report to a named body. Near-miss rate is not tracked.
rows.B_note: Survey metrics tracked against targets (EV-133), but no evidence of interventions triggered by dips or repeated cycles

rows.A_note: Level 2 is met: EV-140 (intake), EV-141 (monthly review), EV-142 (bidirectional decision log) and EV-143 (response process, with the unanswered backlog recorded). The monthly review is minuted 9 of 9, but it reviews items, not metrics against targets, so the artefact that distinguishes level 3 is absent.
rows.B_note: Feedback metrics reviewed on cadence (EV-141), but no real-time/public transparency or repeated influence

rows.A_note: Level 0 does not apply because EV-171 shows dated individual academic contact (a 2026 co-authored paper) with no institutional agreement. That is level 1 by the anchor's own wording. The conference paper sits slightly awkwardly against anchor 1's 'no publication' clause, but agreement and knowledge-exchange are both missing, which keeps the level at 1.
rows.B_note: EV-170 states no partnership, agreement, or programme exists; only informal contact evidenced (EV-171)

rows.A_note: Level 2 is met: all 5 top-ranked risks have plans with options, a named owner and a date (EV-640). Quarterly status review (EV-642) is not a metric against target. The overdue vendor-concentration plan is re-dated, not a level-2 failure.
rows.B_note: Completion-versus-plan and residual-risk reduction metrics reviewed each cycle (EV-642), but no effectiveness measurement or plan revision

rows.A_note: EV-660 and EV-661 show a high-quality level-2 example for VIC-2, but coverage is partial, so the score is 1. The template amendment is intent for SDE and LDA, which is not rewarded.
rows.B_note: Options analysis and rationale for 4 of 6 systems (EV-660, EV-661, EV-662), but no review of redirected/rejected proposals

rows.A_note: Level 2 is met for all six systems. Level 3 fails the MEASURE and CADENCE tests: a quarterly interval exists, but there is no target, no named body and no next date. Level 4 has no predictive or automated artefact.
rows.B_note: Level 3 satisfied: maintenance plan and value metrics tracked and reviewed quarterly for all systems, with decisions recorded. No evidence of predictive modelling or automated optimisation.

rows.A_note: The procedure is system-agnostic and was applied to two different systems' incidents. The set does not state an explicit scope register, so the level 2 coverage clause is accepted on that basis only. Level 3 measurement is absent; the procedure changes in EV-682 are not predictive or automated, so level 4 is not reached.
rows.B_note: Level 3 satisfied: emergent-risk detections, response times and lessons closed measured and reviewed per cycle, with procedure changes recorded. No evidence of predictive detection or automated response.

rows.A_note: The critical vendors are well monitored (quarterly schedule, issues logged and closed, one open with owner and date). Coverage is partial (3 of 6 vendors), so the score is level 1. No contractual-threshold review is named for level 3.
rows.B_note: Level 2 satisfied: monitoring schedule, controls applied, performance tracked, issues logged and closed for critical vendors. No coverage for all vendors, so level 3 fails.

rows.A_note: Level 2 is met: every release in the log cites its trigger. Throughput is reported quarterly, but the measured-effect clause fails coverage. No external recognition is named for level 4.
rows.B_note: Level 3 satisfied: improvement throughput and measured effect per release tracked and reported. No evidence of optimisation or external recognition.

rows.A_note: Communication and notification are well evidenced (EV-741, EV-742, with the breach recorded), but a level 2 clause lacks its own artefact, so the score is level 1. The level 3 metrics cannot lift the score past that.
rows.B_note: Level 3 satisfied: incident metrics (counts, time-to-notify, recurrence) reviewed on cadence, notification performance reported. No evidence of incident-driven change or automated detection.

rows.A_note: The framework (EV-210) is documented but covers role families, not each project. Coverage is 4 of 6, so the score is level 1. Level 3 composition-versus-requirement metrics are absent.
rows.B_note: Level 2 satisfied: documented competency requirements per project, team composition reviewed against them, gaps recorded. No metrics tracked or reported.

rows.A_note: EV-220 ties the four themes to the mission, but the review is asserted rather than evidenced by minutes. KPIs (EV-222) belong to level 3 and cannot lift the score past a failed level 2.
rows.B_note: Level 3 satisfied: strategic KPIs tracked and reported to board on cadence. No evidence of strategy revisions traceable to KPI movement.

rows.A_note: VIC-2 is well evidenced, including realised 22% versus modelled 25%, but that is one system. Coverage fails, so the score is level 1.
rows.B_note: Level 2 satisfied: business case with value metrics and post-deployment value tracking for most systems, but not all.

rows.A_note: The L2/L3 distinguishing artefact (EV-242) is present, but it fails the coverage test (2 of 4 tolerances). The Q3 report's breach dated 2026-05 falls in Q2, which is an unresolved inconsistency. Score held at ML3.
rows.B_note: Level 3 satisfied: exposures tracked against tolerance on cadence, breach escalated. Level 4 requires evidence of tolerance re-setting after breach, not present.

rows.A_note: VIC-2 alone meets level 2 content. Level 3 fails regardless, because no coverage or escape metrics are named. The choice is between ML2 and ML3 depending on scope, which the set cannot establish, so NA rather than 0.
rows.B_note: Methodology and TEVV plan documented and reviewed, but no evidence of metrics review per release.

rows.A_note: Level 3 fails regardless: EV-302 records a single quarter's actuals, with no two minuted reviews and no next date. The score is therefore ML2 or lower, and the set cannot say which, so NA.
rows.B_note: Total-cost model and non-monetary costs documented for VIC-2 only.

rows.A_note: Per-release checks occurred and one drift was re-scoped, but the MEASURE definition is unmet. The L3 distinguishing artefact is present but fails the measure test, so the score is held at ML3. The anchor for level 2 does not require per-system coverage.
rows.B_note: Scope-drift checks measured per release and acted upon, but no evidence of automated drift detection.

rows.A_note: The inspector role meets level 2 content: a standard, recorded assessments for 38 of 38, and a certification step. Level 3 fails regardless, since there is no threshold or report. The choice between ML2 and ML3 depends on role coverage, which cannot be established from the set.
rows.B_note: Formal requirements, assessment, and certification process evidenced; tracking/reporting not evidenced.

rows.A_note: The L1 anchor expressly places a procedure that does not cite the policy clause at level 1. The effectiveness assessment is a single occurrence, the first one (2026-08), so no cadence exists. Override, review and agreement rates are not reported per system.
rows.B_note: Oversight procedure, log, and effectiveness assessment evidenced; measurement/reporting of rates not evidenced.

rows.A_note: The map is documented and reviewed quarterly, but the level 2 coverage test fails on an open exception. No coverage or reassessment metrics are named for level 3.
rows.B_note: Systematic mapping and legal review for most vendors; tracking metrics and closure to plan not evidenced.

rows.A_note: EV-360 and EV-361 show a documented assessment that fed a Steering Committee decision for VIC-2, which is well above level 1 for that system. The open exception (3 systems) blocks level 2. There is no coverage or mitigation-completion metric, so level 3 is also unsupported.
rows.B_note: Evidence shows impact assessment and stakeholder input feeding decision for VIC-2 and PDM, but coverage is incomplete (SDE, LDA, QAP overdue) and no mitigation-completion metric is tracked.

rows.A_note: Level 2: EV-420 (charter scope and audit plan), EV-421 (signed independence statement) and EV-422 (independence recorded in the engagement letter). External assessors (EV-422) are a level-4-type artefact, but level 3 is missing, so the two-level rule keeps the score at 2.
rows.B_note: External metrology laboratory engaged, independence documented, reports present, programme changes traceable to findings.

rows.A_note: Level 1 is met: EV-530 shows a grouped analysis with 3 metrics. EV-533 (results per release against thresholds) is a level-3 artefact, but level 2 fails on the open Brno disparity, so the score stays at 1. The one-system scope question is secondary because level 2 already fails.
rows.B_note: Fairness results tracked per group and release, mitigations recorded, but no intersectional analysis or public reporting.

rows.A_note: EV-463 shows a threshold re-set with before-and-after alert-to-action time (6.2 h to 3.5 h), but level 4 is unreachable until the level-3 dated report and its named review exist. Level 2 and level 3 boundary: the review cadence artefact is missing.
rows.B_note: Level 4 is satisfied: EV-463 records dated changes to alert thresholds from measured incident data, before-and-after alert-to-action times, and traceability to the motivating report (EV-462).

rows.A_note: Minutes coverage is complete (EV-561), but each clause needs its own artefact and system coverage cannot be inferred from the entry count.
rows.B_note: EV-560, EV-561, EV-562 show log, review, and closure, but do not measure tracking coverage or time-to-log.

rows.A_note: The channel, volume and feedback-to-change log (EV-582) are strong, but the appeal clause is unaddressed, so the score is NA rather than 0 or 1. Establishing that the appeal process exists would support level 2, and establishing that it does not would support 0 or 1.
rows.B_note: EV-580, EV-581, EV-582 show channel, appeal process, and feedback-to-change log, but do not measure volume, outcomes, or resolution times.

rows.A_note: External validation exists (EV-600), but level 4 needs level 3 and the programme revision from disagreements is not evidenced. The Plant Quality Board conflict is noted but mitigated.
rows.B_note: EV-600, EV-601, EV-602 show independent review, coverage, and disagreement resolution, but not external validation with programme revision.

rows.A_note: EV-612 gives the targets (3 and 10 days) and a named body, but per-event recording and the minuted cadence are missing, so level 3 fails. Level 4 is unreachable and no predictive modelling is evidenced.
rows.B_note: EV-610, EV-611, EV-612, EV-613 show detection, root cause, corrective action, measured latency and reporting, but not predictive modelling.
